approaches.name: interoperable digital government platforms and analytics for statistics, tax, planning and audit
approaches.description: The project builds interoperable data platforms, analytics tools and automated systems across statistics, revenue, planning, procurement and audit agencies to digitize government processes. Practices: Integrated National Statistical System with interoperable open data ecosystem; Advanced data analytics tools digitizing the government data life cycle; web-based data dissemination platform for microdata and indicators; data analytics and automation system for tax administration; end-to-end automated income tax business processes; interoperable revenue administration systems architecture; automated taxpayer call center; upgraded PPS platform integrated with e-PMIS; microservices-based unified planning platform with analytics; MYPIP/GCR tools embedded in upgraded PPS; API interoperability between PPS, AMS and e-PMIS; e-GP enhancements for OCDS compliance and budget integration; cloud-ready microservices e-GP 2.0 deployment study; FIMA digital campus / virtual learning hub with sector-specific digital content for OCAG auditor professionalization; API-based interoperable audit data infrastructure with AI audit; Centralized data analytics tool integrated with five government IT systems; Blockchain-based audit interface for decentralized auditees; Real-time AI/ML audit and e-vouching verification; IT audit system interfacing with e-GP procurement data; Digital platform integrated with iBAS++ for financial statements; digital microdata downloads from BBS platforms; digitized Project Preparation and Appraisal System integrated with Planning Division IT; website analytics tracking microdata downloads from BBS; CAAT and AI/ML-based audit analytics interfaced with government IT systems.
approaches.why_innovative: New delivery arrangement: integrated NSS producing and openly sharing interoperable official statistics | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 2 round(s); context expanded; final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Subcomponent 1.1.1 (US$6 million) aims to integrate official statistics into the government’s digital data agenda by establishing an integrated NSS that produces and enables sharing and use of reliable official statistics to improve policy making and service delivery and (b) supporting a transparent data ecosystem by ensuring that key data are open, accessible, and interoperable.

extra_evidence.text: This component, to be implemented by BBS, complements the transparency reforms supported by the SGIR DPC through the adoption of digital data ecosystems and statistical capacity enhancement and modernization.

This objective will be achieved through (a) investing in advanced data analytical tools to improve the use of indicators and microdata across government and tap into new data sources to produce next-generation indicators and microdata and support the integration of data sources and the application of data analytics to digitize the data life cycle and (b) enhancing coordination and data governance across agencies and strengthen and clarify roles and responsibilities around Governmentwide data leadership.6 Building on existing memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with administrative data-producing agencies within the NSS, the project will operationalize and enhance the efficacy of data sharing across these agencies while also establishing new MoUs with additional agencies.

(c) improving data dissemination platforms for timely and regularly updated web-based access to statistical publications, microdata, and time series indicators;9 (d) establishing mechanisms for systematic citizen engagement through user- producer dialogue, including organizing Data Users Forums to monitor and promote improved data transparency and access; and (e) supporting statistical capacity building at the division, zilla, and upazila levels to meet the growing demand for subnational economic statistics.

With the impending separation of tax policy making from administration and streamlining of tax expenditures under the SGIR DPC, substantial capacity- building efforts have been planned to develop a robust data analytics and automation system, which is essential for successfully implementing these reforms.

The subcomponent will strengthen the capacity of NBR’s Research and Statistics Wing in data collection, management, tax analysis, revenue forecasting, tax gap and tax expenditure analysis, and identification of compliance risks.
It will support (a) income tax administration digitalization and upgradation, including end-to-end automation of simplified business processes;

(c) development of an overall systems architecture for revenue administration systems and interoperability among the NBR IT systems (Automated System for Customs Data [ASYCUDA] World, IVAS, and income tax) and with the Integrated Budgeting and Accounting System (iBAS++), and other key data systems;
Page 8 The World Bank Strengthening Institutions for Transparency and Accountability (SITA) (P506691) outreach and services, including the establishment of an automated taxpayer call center.

This would include a substantial upgrading of the Project Processing Appraisal and Management System (PPS) platform, ensuring seamless integration with other Planning Division systems and full integration with IMED's e-PMIS.
Currently, data exchange between the PPS and other Planning Division systems is minimal, and there is no comprehensive data analysis or reporting in place.
(b) system design using a microservices-based approach, ensuring compatibility with existing systems and databases, and incorporating advanced data analytics capabilities;
(c) development of data analytics and business intelligence for decision-making; and (d) upgrading IT systems based on user feedback.
The goal is to integrate the Planning Division systems into a unified platform, enabling robust interoperability, scalable services, and efficient data exchange.

The project will facilitate the development of the Multi-Year Public Investment Program (MYPIP) integrated with the Medium-Term Budget Framework (MTBF), as well as the development and monitoring of GCR indicators, resource allocation, and spending.
MYPIP/GCR tools will be part of the PPS during its upgradation, and the project will also update the GCR development guideline 2023 of the Planning Division and provide training on MYPIP/GCR.

These digital tools will include the development of Application Programming Interface (API) and interoperability mechanisms to ensure seamless data exchange between PPS, AMS, and e-PMIS (Project Management Information System) platforms.
(d) Open Contracting Data Standards (OCDS) compliance;
(e) upstream integration of APP with the IBAS++ Budget module;
(f) security upgrade from symmetric to more secure hybrid of latest symmetric and asymmetric encryption; and (g) data center upgrade.

The project will finance detailed study to evaluate the system design options, cloud deployment readiness, microservices architecture, business process reengineering, and user experience assessment to improve public procurement efficiency.
The outputs from this study will be used to procure and deploy the upgraded Bangladesh e- Procurement system version 2.0 with this project financing.

The Financial Management Academy (FIMA) will be transformed into a digitalized learning hub for all OCAG officials, so that OCAG can produce audit Page 12 The World Bank Strengthening Institutions for Transparency and Accountability (SITA) (P506691) reports in a timely manner with relevant and impactful accountability issues, and other governance institutions in the country can leverage the published reports of OCAG.

Hence, to fill the gap, the subcomponent will expand the IT infrastructure for OCAG’s in-house operation, data storage, interoperability, and data networking within OCAG offices and other government digital systems for revenue, expenditure and debt, audit management, API-based data sharing, data mining and AI based audit, verification, inspection and investigation, and public interface for open data to citizens.

(d) developing and integrating a centralized data analytics tool with five main IT systems maintained by other government institutions (including IBAS++, IVAS, e-GP, ASYCUDA, the Integrated Tax Administration System [ITAS], Land, and Bangladesh Road and Transport Authority [BRTA]);

(c) building real-time audit capacity to respond with greater agility through innovative IT-based techniques, such as machine learning, technology- facilitated verification, inspection, disruptive technology and artificial intelligence for big data analysis, e-vouching, and verification;

(f) building digital interface and capacity in OCAG to facilitate audit leveraging emerging technologies like blockchain implemented in entities (auditee) with decentralized operation; and (g)conducting stakeholder engagement with other digitally operated PFM institutions and systems so that the access, data sharing, and interoperability with OCAG remain at an optimum level.

(f) an IT audit system interfacing with e-procurement (e-GP) and procurement audits of infrastructure investments; and (g) activities relating to implementation of the proposed Audit Act upon its enactment including framing of rules, audit of assets and liabilities, stores and stock, revenues, and receipts.

Hence the component will provide a digital platform integrated with iBAS++ that will support (a) Comptroller General of Accounts and Self Accounting Entities in preparing timely financial statements in accordance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards, codes, and standards and thus it will facilitate the timely submission of annual audited financial statements ;

Specifically, the project will enhance public access to official statistics and microdata through digital data downloads from BBS platforms and improve digital service delivery at NBR by increasing online return submissions for both Income Tax and VAT.

The proposed project will contribute to the corporate scorecard indicator “People using digitally enabled services” by supporting the expansion and uptake of digital platforms across key government institutions.
